title: Dimension shifting for Tor along a free presentation
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $0\to K\xrightarrow{j}F\xrightarrow{p}M\to0$ a short exact sequence of $R$-modules with $F$ a free $R$-module, and $N$ an $R$-module. Then for every integer $i\ge1$ there is an isomorphism of $R$-modules $\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,N)$, with $\operatorname{Tor}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. In particular $\operatorname{Tor}^R_2(M,N)=0$ if and only if $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(K,N)=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), line 35476: 'Since $N^0$ is free, we also see that $\text{Tor}_2^B(H^0, C) = \text{Tor}_1^B(M, C)$' (stated there without proof); the definition used is Algebra, Section Tag 00LY (section-tor, lines 18215--18236) with Lemma Tag 00LZ (lemma-tor-welldefined, line 18239) for the independence of the resolution, which gives the proof by splicing a free resolution of K with F. Tags verified in tags/tags: 00S2,algebra-lemma-exact-sequence-NL; 00LY,algebra-section-tor; 00LZ,algebra-lemma-tor-welldefined

proof.text: Apply the already proved natural dimension-shifting theorem [lem-sc-p1-tor-dimension-shift-natural] to S and each i >= 1. Evaluate its family of isomorphisms at the given N and retain the isomorphism, obtaining the first conjunct. Its hypotheses are exactly the commutative ring, short exact sequence, and free middle module assumed here.

Specialize the first conjunct to i = 1 to obtain e : Tor_2(S.X3,N) ≅ Tor_1(S.X1,N). If the source is zero, transport zero-ness along e.symm using Mathlib Limits.IsZero.of_iso; if the target is zero, transport along e. Pair these implications to obtain the second conjunct.
